events.summary:
Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week

Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.

After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s strongest condemnation of the continued Iranian aggression against its territory, including the attack launched today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, by drones that were intercepted and destroyed by air defense systems in the Kingdom’s airspace.

This comes two days after a similar attack at dawn on Friday, November 13, 2026, by two drones that were also intercepted. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard explicitly claimed responsibility for these attacks. The Ministry praised the efficiency, vigilance, and capability of the Bahrain Defense Force in confronting today’s attack and its complete readiness to deter any aggression.
The Ministry considered these attacks a resumption of Iran’s heinous aggression against the Kingdom and countries in the region, disregarding the provisions of international law and the principles of the UN Charter.

events.summary:
Prime ministerial hopeful calls Arab minority ‘an integral part of the Israeli story’ as he seeks to form government

Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot condemned a “racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation” against the country’s Arab citizens, after the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, accused Arab parties of electoral fraud without evidence.

Netanyahu has repeatedly targeted Arab parties and Palestinian citizens of Israel after his party received a disappointing electoral showing, accusing them of manipulating the election and being linked to Hamas. Israeli electoral authorities have rejected these claims as not being backed by evidence.

events.title: Iran says it targeted US military radar in Bahrain in retaliatory strike
events.summary:
First direct attack on US military installations for months was in response to US airstrike on communications tower

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months.

“This is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the strait of Hormuz,” the IRGC said. “In the event of repeated violations and aggression, the IRGC aerospace force is on full alert to confront the enemy without constraint.”

events.title: Boxer on death row in Iran vows ‘not to bow before oppression’ after winning rights prize
events.summary:
Political prisoner Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran, given prestigious Magnitsky humanitarian award

A boxer and political prisoner on death row in Iran said he will “never surrender” as he accepted a prestigious human rights prize on behalf of “the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives”.

Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, an Iranian boxing champion, coach and political prisoner, has been sentenced to death three times and is one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran. He was given the Magnitsky award for outstanding human rights activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday night.

events.title: Two men found guilty of helping Iran try to ‘eliminate’ UK-based journalists
events.summary:
Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi Manesh carried out surveillance in an effort to inflict violence on targets

Two men of Iranian origin who were hired through social media as part of a plan to “eliminate” journalists in the UK have been found guilty of assisting Tehran’s intelligence services.

Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, carried out surveillance and reconnaissance between August 2024 and March last year in an attempt to inflict violence on “subjects” in the UK.

events.summary:
International court of justice has never before found a state guilty of genocide, and ruling will have implications for case against Israel

The world’s top court will deliver a judgment this week on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, in a landmark case that will set a critical 21st-century benchmark for the gravest of all international crimes.

The closely watched judgment could become one of the most significant moments in international law since the end of the second world war.

events.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh from exile
events.summary:
Former prime minister faces death penalty upon return after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in 2024 uprising

Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week.

Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.

events.title: Grenades, grief and a deepening political divide: five takeaways from Sonia Gandhi’s new memoir

The former’s much-awaited political memoir, Belonging, offers a strikingly candid account of her journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of power in India – all for love, she says.

The veteran Congress party leader has been fiercely protective of her personal world. Mumbai facility is part of Reliance Industries, owner of world’s biggest oil refinery and funder of controversial mega-zoo

The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo.

A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.

events.title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’
events.summary:
A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years

It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator.

Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.

events.summary:
Four arrested after BMW collides with Volkswagen on Gelderd Road, with police appealing for witnesses

Two people aged 22 and 23 have died after their car was hit by a BMW being pursued by police.

West Yorkshire police said four people had been arrested after the crash in Leeds on Sunday and appealed for witnesses to come forward.

events.summary:
Exclusive: South Wales police figures show BAME people accounted for 24% of selected scans in 2025, despite being 7% of population

Ethnic minority people are four times more likely than their white counterparts to be chosen for some police facial scans, according to official data, sparking warnings of racial bias.

events.summary:

Poundland’s under-fire US owners have released funds to help the stricken discount chain restock shelves temporarily, keeping hopes of a rescue deal alive in the run-up to crunch talks with the government.

events.summary:

Cold weather warnings have been issued for parts of the UK, and alerts for the risk to health services are due to begin on Sunday evening.

The Met Office issued yellow weather warnings for ice for central and eastern Scotland from 6pm on Sunday evening until 10am on Monday. People should be vigilant as they travelled, due to the risk from slipping on footpaths in icy conditions, it added.

events.summary:
From Aldi candles to Quince’s cashmere jumpers, cheaper dupes of high-end goods have gone mainstream. But is it fair?

For fans of the festive season nothing is more Christmassy than lighting a super-sized botanical candle with its trim of orange slices and berries.

In a statement, the Trump administration-led FAA said the wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a United Parcel Service Boeing 767 “while the airplanes were taxiing at Miami International Airport”.

events.summary:

Donald Trump’s legal and political ploys to increase his wealth and boost Republican electoral prospects have fueled lawsuits by non-partisan groups, prompting federal judges to issue stinging rejections to some of the president’s schemes.

Several lawsuits were filed in 2026 against Trump’s schemes to benefit his bottom line by reducing potential tax liabilities, boosting his Truth Social platform financially by offering big investors early access to his posts, and helping Republicans by using federal funds to pay for highly partisan ads touting Trump’s record in the run-up to the midterm elections, in which Republicans suffered a heavy defeat.

The Trump administration is finalizing a rule to reimburse doctors who diagnose, treat and counsel patients with side effects from vaccines in what experts believe is an attempt to undermine trust in vaccines and to create an evidence base on their purported risks.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), also announced the creation of a vaccine “injury” research center at the National Institutes of Health and has sought to reshape the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP) – actions that point to Kennedy’s longtime activism against vaccination as well as the profits he and his network have made from vaccine lawsuits.

SpaceX’s megarocket Starship returned to its Texas launch tower on Saturday, a milestone in the company’s efforts to make the craft suitable for human spaceflight.

events.summary: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

events.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
events.summary: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

events.title: New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
events.summary: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.

events.title: Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
events.summary: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.

events.title: Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors
events.summary: The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."

events.title: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?
events.summary: Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?

events.title: Germany: CDU names Ilse Aigner as candidate for president
events.summary: The steering committtee of the CDU have announced Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as presidential candidate. This gives her a good chance of becoming the first woman to occupy the role.

events.title: EU aims to pick new ECB chief by year-end
events.summary: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as head of the European Central Bank (ECB) has put the European Union on a tight schedule. The bloc expects to pick a new ECB chief by the end of December.

events.title: Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race
events.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an affair with a woman the US believes was spying for China. The story could have profound implications for the world's most valuable company and the global AI race.

events.title: Who is Ilse Aigner, leading candidate for Germany's next president?
events.summary: She would be the first female president and the first Christian Social Union politician to hold Germany's highest office. Ilse Aigner is the favored candidate for the Federal Convention vote on January 30.

events.title: Germany news: Germany marks fateful date of November 9
events.summary: Germany is commemorating the Nazi-led November pogroms 88 years ago. Events are also being held to mark the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989. DW has more.

events.title: Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
events.summary: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.

events.title: Germany: Chancellor Merz to nominate Aigner for president
events.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for federal president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.

events.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
events.summary: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

events.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?

events.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
events.summary: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

events.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
events.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

events.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
events.summary: German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.

events.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
events.summary: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

events.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
events.summary: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

events.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
events.summary: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

events.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
events.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

events.title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
events.summary: Political debate about the recent Gen Z riots have raised the question: Can Germany talk about problems with integration without putting entire groups of people under suspicion?

events.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
events.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

events.title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
events.summary: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.

events.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
events.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

events.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
events.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

events.title: The 2011 discovery of neo-Nazi killers aired biases in German policing
events.summary: Many questions still surround the National Socialist Underground whose existence was revealed by neo-Nazi terrorist Beate Zschäpe on November 4, 2011. How has German society reacted to NSU crimes? Has justice been done?

events.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
events.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

events.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
events.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

events.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
events.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

events.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
events.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

events.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
events.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

events.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
events.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

events.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
events.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

events.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
events.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

events.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
events.summary: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.

events.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
events.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

events.title: Germany news: Ukraine in focus at Berlin Security Conference
events.summary: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.

events.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
events.summary: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.

events.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
events.summary: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

events.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
events.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.

events.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
events.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

events.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
events.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

events.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

events.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
events.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

events.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

events.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

events.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
events.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

events.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
events.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

events.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
events.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

events.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
events.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

events.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
events.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

events.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
events.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

events.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
events.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

events.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
events.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

events.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
events.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

events.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
events.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

events.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
events.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

events.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
events.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

events.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
events.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

events.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
events.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

events.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
events.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

events.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
events.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

events.title: Iran claims drone attack on US military base in Bahrain
events.summary: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama. It comes after Iran targeted an airbase in the US-allied island state, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East War and comes as negotiations to end the conflict remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

events.title: Canaries urge government action after 2,200 migrants reach the islands in 48h
events.summary: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The Spanish islands are one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants from Africa. The Spanish Interior Ministry says more than 13,000 arrived there between January and the end of last month. Details and analysis by Andrew Hilliar, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.

events.title: Jensen Huang: The French Connection
events.summary: President Trump is heading to Asia in a few days time, and will meet President Putin and President Xi. There's likely to be one fewer tech giants at the table, Jensen Huang, newly resigned from Nvidia, over the suspected spy affair.

events.title: Santa school in full swing in London ahead of Christmas celebrations
events.summary: It may still be November but it's beginning to look a lot like Christmas in South London, as many Santa impersonators are heading to school for their festive training. The school, organised by an event company called Ministry of Fun, brings together Santas, elves, and Mrs Clauses to share experiences, practice belly laughs and learn how to bring the magic of Christmas to life. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

events.title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
events.summary: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.

events.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is bad news for Europe’s AI ambitions
events.summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang poured money into open-source AI, from French-founded Hugging Face to chips for Mistral's data centres, and fought Washington's attempts to restrict it. With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed.

events.title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
events.summary: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.

events.title: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
events.summary: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. The scandal has also raised questions about how much the US government knew – Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not react. Analysis by Laïla Mörch, CEO of Shael and tech investor in Paris.

events.title: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly
events.summary: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images, from angry protests over a housing crisis that has dominated Spain's election campaign, to Leo XIV's visit to his adopted homeland Peru and "Rocky" fans marking 50 years since the release of boxing movie classic.

events.title: French Ciryl Gane retains MMA heavyweaight title agianst Josh Hokit
events.summary: Ciryl Gane remains the world's MMA heavyweight champion. Overnight, the French athlete beat Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in ​New York. The 5-round fight was rough, as Shirli Sitbon explains.

events.title: Bahrain says air defences destroyed several Iranian drones attacking US base
events.summary: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September. The second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war. Diplomatic efforts to end the almost nine-month conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, with ​sporadic attacks continuing. Details from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Tehran, Reza Sayah.

events.title: France's presidential race heats up
events.summary: In approximately six months time, French voters will head to the polls for the first round of the presidential election.  Due to term limits, current president Emmanuel Macron is barred from running again. But that hasn't stopped a whole host of candidates from tossing their hat in the ring.

events.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russia's petrochemical capital in overnight assault
events.summary: Russian officials confirmed Sunday that the central industrial city of Nizhnekamsk had endured "prolonged" Ukrainian airstrikes overnight, damaging a residential building and sparking a fire at a major petrochemical complex, injuring three people. Separate overnight strikes on Taganrog city killed an electricity substation engineer, according to the regional governor.

events.title: The Philippines and Australia strengthen joint military deterrence at ASEAN summit
events.summary: Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in the Philippine capital Manila on Sunday. During three days, world leaders are expected to focus on trade, energy and conflict – including the war in Iran. Donald Trump is expected to land in Manila on Tuesday. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Bangkok Tommy Walker.

events.title: Will Ukraine make territorial concessions for NATO membership?
events.summary: The United States suggested Ukraine make territorial concessions in exchange for a NATO membership, according to Volodymyr Zelensky. The Ukrainian president also claims that Russia has rejected an energy truce. This week’s US-mediated negotiations did not result in any tangible progress. Story by Simon Moritz.

events.title: Air travel issues persist in the US after nationwide ground stop
events.summary: After almost five hours of grounded flights in the US, flights have resumed. However, passengers are still waiting and wading through tough logistics to get to their destinations after massive delays and cancelled flights. Details by Simon Moritz.

events.title: Francophone summit opens in Cambodia, overshadowed by tensions in Africa
events.summary: The 20th Francophonie Summit opened on Sunday in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, overshadowed by a high-stakes leadership dispute. The International Organisation of the Francophonie is set to elect its next secretary-general on Monday for a four-year term, but escalating friction between Rwanda, which has led the OIF for eight years, and the Democratic Republic of Congo has thrown the summit into crisis. Details by Liza Kaminov.

events.title: Illegal mining threatens French Guiana forests and indigenous communities
events.summary: In French Guiana, the fight against illegal gold mining is rapidly being lost and creating an environmental and health disaster, according to the World Wildlife Fund. During an aerial survey in early August, park rangers counted 239 illegal sites within the protected area in record.

events.title: Are we too reliant on technology? Questions arise after Microsoft's widespread outages
events.summary: This week's Microsoft outage highlighted the risks of relying on a single technology provider for essential services. The disruption lasted nearly 24 hours, impacting millions of users across more than 70 countries – from government agencies to airlines to hospitals and small businesses. Are we too reliant on technology? Analysis by Marcel Saucet, research associate at the University of San Diego School of Law.

events.title: Pope laments poverty-stricken Inca communities as locals leave Peru
events.summary: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday will traverse the length of Peru in what marks the penultimate day of his Latin American tour. The leader of the Catholic church – who underwent cancer surgery just a month ago – warned that Peru's remote Inca communities are under threat as poverty continues to drive locals out of their homeland in search of better futures.

events.title: Global diesel prices ease as winter approaches
events.summary: Global diesel prices, which have remained elevated since the start of the Iran war and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, have fallen sharply in recent weeks as Gulf exports recover and global oil supplies get back on track for the first time since February. The price drop is being felt in Europe, where prices remain roughly 77% above pre-war levels, and in the US, where the national average fell below $6 a gallon on Saturday. Details by Liza Kaminov.

events.title: Philippine star Carmelle wins first Asian edition of Eurovision song contest
events.summary: The Philippines has won the first Asian edition of the Eurovision Song Contest. The Filipino singer beat ten other acts to take the title in Bangkok, with a song celebrating women's empowerment. A taste of the winning song with Jack Pownall.

events.title: Iran claims attack on US military airbase in Bahrain
events.summary: Iranian military confirmed on Sunday an attack on a US military base in Bahrain, in its second targeting the Middle Eastern country in the space of three days. Bahrain's military said it had intercepted several Iranian attacks, with the foreign ministry confirming its air defence systems had shot down Iranian drones, preventing them from reaching their intended targets.

events.title: SpaceX makes rocketry history by recapturing massive reusable rocketship
events.summary: After failing to catch a booster yesterday, SpaceX managed to recapture its massive reusable rocketship, "Starship" for the first time. Smaller previous models have successfully relanded but they require heavy legs and aren't fully reusable. Story by Daniel Quinlan.

events.title: US asked if Ukraine would give up parts of Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskyy says
events.summary: The US has asked for the first time whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the Donbas region if Kyiv were admitted to NATO, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

events.title: Hamas says senior commander killed in Israeli airstrike

events.title: Megaspeed, chip firm at center of Nvidia scandal, pledges to cooperate with U.S. investigation
events.summary: HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said Thursday it will cooperate with the U.S. government’s investigations into the matter.

events.title: U.S. charges 3 men with plotting multiple terror attacks, including on British air base
events.summary: One of the men helped direct the planned attack against the air base while he was in a U.S. prison, according to a Justice Department indictment.

events.title: Senior U.S. Army soldier arrested in U.K. on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
events.summary: The 41-year-old man was arrested “as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing” near the ⁠city of Gloucester, ​in the west ⁠of England, British police said.

events.title: U.S. moves military aircraft from British base amid Iran threats
events.summary: A U.S. official confirmed to NBC News that several military aircraft had left RAF Mildenhall as the security posture there had increased.

events.title: Nvidia opens investigation after CEO’s affair with alleged Chinese spy
events.summary: Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in an employee memo. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

events.title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assaults
events.summary: The 51-year-old comedian and actor was found guilty in a British court last week.

events.title: Gunman with far-right views who killed 6 in Poland shooting rampage dies in hospital
events.summary: The man, described as being his mid-20s, was shot by police during Saturday’s attack in the main square of Poland’s second-largest city.

events.title: Parents, sister of far-right Kraków shooter found dead in family home
events.summary: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków, Poland, belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.

events.title: Gunman kills 6 in ‘terror attack’ in Poland, officials say; 3 others found dead in his home
events.summary: A gunman described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs fatally shot six people while driving through a public square Saturday in Krakow, Poland, officials said, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.” Three of his relatives were later found dead in his home.

events.title: Pope Leo, who had cancer surgery weeks ago, begins South American tour
events.summary: Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.

events.title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
events.summary: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown.

events.title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
events.summary: No explosives have been found, and it isn’t clear who or what is behind the calls, but the threats alone have caused chaos in the skies and airports.

events.title: Clashes erupt in France as ‘Black Thursday’ protests sweep the nation
events.summary: “Everything is going up except wages and pensions,” the country’s main unions said. “Anger is immense.”

events.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
events.summary: Six women alleged that the British comedian had sexually assaulted them at his home, in hotels and public bathrooms. Brand has denied all claims.

events.title: Melania Trump calls for ‘enduring’ Russia-Ukraine peace as she hosts top officials at the White House
events.summary: Ukraine has been reeling from the worst collapse in relations with Washington since the start of the war.
